claim: A 4x KV cache size reduction incurs no accuracy degradation from 7B parameters up, and a compressed model is more accurate than a smaller uncompressed model with the same cache size.
stance_target: The claim that KV compression can be obtained without architectural sparse attention
scope_conditions: Instruction-following and reasoning evaluations; Qwen2.5 model family from 7B up
quoted_support: A 4x cache size reduction incurs no accuracy degradation from 7B parameters up, and a compressed model is more accurate than a smaller uncompressed model with the same cache size.

claim: On Qwen2.5-14B at 16k context, 4x cache compression composed with eviction to one position in eight yields a 32x smaller decode-time cache while preserving accuracy — the two ratios multiply.
stance_target: How far post-hoc KV compression can go when composed with eviction
quoted_support: On Qwen2.5-14B at 16k, a 4x compression due to our cache configuration plus eviction to one position in eight gives a 32x smaller cache at decode

claim: The paper's framing is that these results support pre-training large models and compressing them only afterwards — i.e. substantial KV compression is a post-hoc operation, not a reason to adopt sparse attention during pretraining.
stance_target: The premise that CSA2-style architectural KV compression is required to make long-context training affordable
quoted_support: Together, these findings support pre-training large models and compressing them only afterwards.

claim: Applying any single compression axis uniformly across all layers limits achievable compression because it degrades accuracy; composing mild settings locally and adaptively across depth, precision and rank preserves accuracy at much higher compression.
stance_target: The claim that uniform KV compression (e.g. one global bit-width) is the wrong design
quoted_support: We observe that these interventions taken independently and uniformly over all layers limit achievable compression because they degrade accuracy. Crucially, composing them locally and adaptively to the context can instead preserve accuracy while achieving large memory savings.

claim: The selector runs once at the start of prefill and its choice then holds for every generated token, so the compression decision costs one forward pass of a small selector rather than per-token overhead.
stance_target: The runtime cost of adaptive KV compression
quoted_support: During inference, the selector runs once at the start of pre-fill, and its choice then holds for every generated token.

claim: The selector chooses among 17 actions per layer (16 width-precision pairs plus an inherit/reuse action), and the budget can itself be an input so one selector serves several compression targets.
stance_target: The design space of per-layer KV compression choices
scope_conditions: Action space definition; precision in {2,4,8,16} bits
quoted_support: That gives the selector 17 actions per layer as illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The theoretical maximal compression for a 48-layer model such as Qwen2.5-14B is 4108x (8x precision x 10.7 lowest rank x 48 depth), though all experiments target far lower factors.
stance_target: The upper bound on post-hoc KV compression
quoted_support: In theory, the maximal compression factor that could be attained for a 48 layers model such as Qwen2.5-14B could be in practice 8x (precision) times 10.7 (lowest rank), and depth 48, by reusing the first KV layer at all subsequent layers (Table 5). This would yield a maximal compression of 4108x, though all of our experiments target far lower factors.

claim: Selectors trained jointly with the model reach the Pareto frontier of accuracy against cache size, beating learning-free and post-hoc baselines, and the model adapts to the cache it will be served under because selector and model are trained together.
stance_target: Whether adaptive compression needs training-time adaptation
scope_conditions: Supervised fine-tuning with the selector; instruction-following and reasoning tasks
quoted_support: In evaluations on instruction following and reasoning tasks, our selectors reach the Pareto frontier of accuracy against cache size, against learning-free and post-hoc baselines. ... Since we train selector and model together, the model adapts to the cache it will be served under.
